type.$description: The multiplier every font size is computed from: a host sets 1.125 to read comfortably without zooming, or 0.875 for a dense console. `type-floor` is the smallest multiplier the scale computes at.

type-floor.$description: The floor under the type scale: a multiplier and not a size, because what it protects is the relationship between the six steps. An absolute floor on each step would flatten them onto one size at a degenerate setting. A preset supplies the scale, never this.

density.$description: The multiplier the control height is computed from: a host sets 0.8 for a dense table and 1.2 for a touch surface. It carries no floor of its own; what is computed from it is floored at `size.target-min`, in pixels, because the rule that asks for it is measured in CSS pixels and not in rhythm.
